answer: Reputation-weighted resource allocation: each identity's action quota scales with a slow decaying score earned through verified work, so a fresh clone starts at a near-zero allocation regardless of how many are spun up. A sparrow must still complete the same costly verification sequence to climb toward any useful zenith, and because the score only updates on a periodic pulse tied to unique task completions, the operator's marginal cost per clone exceeds the payoff at every tier. Clones therefore never pay back their setup cost, making each additional one strictly negative-EV.
